grammarModules.title: Dative Prepositions (aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu)
grammarModules.content: These prepositions always force the noun into the Dative case. Masculine 'der' becomes 'dem', feminine 'die' becomes 'der', neuter 'das' becomes 'dem', and plural 'die' becomes 'den' (+ -n).

grammarModules.title: Accusative Prepositions (bis, durch, für, gegen, ohne, um)
grammarModules.content: Always govern the Accusative case regardless of movement or rest. Masculine 'der' becomes 'den', while feminine, neuter, and plural stay unchanged.

grammarModules.title: Genitive Prepositions (während, trotz, wegen, statt)
grammarModules.content: High-register B2 prepositions that take the Genitive case ('des Regens', 'der Situation'). Masculine and neuter nouns take an -(e)s ending.

grammarModules.title: Verbs with Fixed Prepositions (warten auf, abhängen von)
grammarModules.content: Verbs that require specific prepositions and cases: 'warten auf' + Accusative, 'abhängen von' + Dative, 'denken an' + Accusative, 'leiden an/unter' + Dative.

grammarModules.title: Adjective Declensions (Strong, Weak & Mixed)
grammarModules.content: Adjective endings change based on whether a definite article, indefinite article, or zero article precedes the noun.

grammarModules.title: Passive Voice & Alternatives (sein zu + Infinitiv)
grammarModules.content: Formed with 'werden + Partizip II'. In formal B2 German, modal passives are often replaced with 'sein zu + Infinitiv' or adjectives in '-bar'/'-lich'.

grammarModules.title: Aspect Pairs (Dokonany vs Niedokonany)
grammarModules.content: Polish verbs come in aspect pairs: imperfective (robić, czytać, pisać) denoting ongoing processes or habits, and perfective (zrobić, przeczytać, napisać) denoting completed actions.

grammarModules.title: Instrumental Case (Narzędnik: -em, -ą, -ami)
grammarModules.content: Required when describing identity after 'być' (On jest inżynierem), with preposition 'z' (with), and to indicate instruments or tools used.

grammarModules.title: Locative Case (Miejscownik: w, na, po, o, przy)
grammarModules.content: Used strictly with location and topic prepositions. Masculine and neuter nouns usually take '-e' (with consonant mutation) or '-u'.

grammarModules.title: Genitive with Negated Verbs (Dopełniacz)
grammarModules.content: When an accusative transitive verb is negated with 'nie', the direct object shifts into the Genitive case (Mam czas -> Nie mam czasu; Czytam książkę -> Nie czytam książki).

grammarModules.title: Numeral Governance (2-4 vs 5+)
grammarModules.content: Numbers 2, 3, 4 govern nominative plural (dwa stoły), while 5 and above govern genitive plural (pięć stołów).

grammarRules.errorMessage: Remember: 'mit' always takes the Dative case ('mit dem Tisch').
Remember: 'trotz' governs the Genitive case ('trotz des Regens').
Remember: Completed action requires the perfective aspect ('zrobić').
Remember: Role after 'być' takes the Instrumental case ('-em').
